reasons: The agent changed the right places. It added a move-to-draft action and button in the wizard logic and summary, and it makes launch replace existing schedules with a fresh active one. That covers both stated requirements in principle. The patch is less robust than upstream, though: the stop gating is loose, and the schedule replacement is not atomic. It also omits the batch-job cancellation and the backend race fix. It is directionally correct but incomplete.

The agent edited the right files and covers the main asks: a Move to draft button and replacing existing schedules on launch. The gating is much looser than upstream. It allows stopping broadcasts that have already sent, which invites duplicate sends on relaunch. It also lacks the in-flight batch job handling, and the schedule replacement is less safe. Right direction but incomplete.

The agent changed the same frontend places as upstream, and the core behavior matches. A live scheduled broadcast now has a "Move to draft" button that sets its status to draft. Launch now deletes existing schedules and creates a fresh active one, which fixes the paused-schedule bug. The gaps are safety edge cases plus the separate backend race fix, so I scored it as functionally equivalent on the request.

results.evidence: moveToDraft calls hogFlowsPartialUpdate(status:'draft') and saveBroadcastFinished, so the broadcast becomes editable. But whether the schedule stops sending while draft is not shown; the schedule isn't touched or paused in the patch. The scheduler behaviour (backend) is not visible. Also scheduleMode after hydrate for live broadcasts is not shown.
canMoveToDraft = broadcast?.status === 'active' && scheduleMode !== 'now'. It relies on scheduleMode, not on a pending schedule; a completed one-time schedule would still show the button.

Existing schedules are listed and destroyed, then one is created, which matches for scheduled sends. But for scheduleMode 'now' no leftover schedules are removed; the destroy is only in the else branch. Also, the status is set active before replacement.

`activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` occurs before the schedule list/destroy/create; the broadcast is marked live first. The catch does revert to draft, but the ordering is not as required.
canMoveToDraft only checks status and scheduleMode; there is no check for in-progress runs, unknown run history, multiple schedules, or workflow shape.
The button's onClick={() => moveToDraft()} acts immediately with no confirmation dialog.
moveToDraft only patches status to draft; no run cancellation and only a single success toast.
The patch has no scheduler/backend change; no status re-verification before run creation.
The new schedule object contains only rrule, starts_at, timezone; old schedules are destroyed without carrying over their variables.

result: `broadcastsLogic.ts` needs no edit. It derives the list status chip from the flow's `status` and batch jobs, so a broadcast moved back to `draft` already shows as draft. The list also reloads when it mounts, so it picks up the change.
